propositions: The parent-first cascade walk is implemented twice: once in claim.py (hardcoded for open parent) and once in transition.py (driven by _CASCADING_EDGES table), creating duplicate logic for ancestor recursion, cycle guarding, TOCTOU re-check, and error rewrap.

The _CASCADING_EDGES decision table must remain single-sourced in transition.py (not moved) because the inbound Gerrit 2044 writer already imports it; only the walk logic should be extracted to a shared module.

A new lifecycle_cascade.py module must expose cascade_parent_first with injected resolve_parent and advance callables, allowing claim and transition to retain their own write primitives while sharing the walk.
All three cascading edges (open→in_progress, closed→open, closed→in_progress) must keep working after extraction; * → closed must continue not cascading.

The inbound status cascade (apply_inbound_events._cascade_inbound_status_parents) deliberately stays separate because its walk returns written event paths topmost-first, an ordering its suite pins that a recursive helper returning None cannot reproduce without complicating the signature.
